title: introduce-budgeted-hush-sampler-and-quant-hinting-for-low-value-requests
author: Ethan Park
commit_summary: feat(prefill): add hush-sampler orchestrator with budgeted sampling lanes
feat(quant): attach quant-hint metadata to sampled requests and expose hint API
chore(test): add canary workload for hush-sampler telemetry and latency assertions
docs: add user guide and ops runbook for hush-sampler and quant hints
ci: add integration smoke test that runs on dedicated staging GPU pool
description: Context and motivation: High-volume low-value requests (status checks, short-answers, autosuggest pings) account for a disproportionate share of prefill and KV cache churn while contributing minimal product value. This PR introduces a 'hush sampler' — a budget-aware, low-priority prefill sampler that reduces prefill frequency for low-value request cohorts and surfaces lightweight quantization-profile hints so downstream serving can select cheaper execution paths when safe. Goals: reduce token-level unit cost for noisy workloads, avoid user-visible regressions for high-value traffic, provide safe fallback and observability for ops. Summary of changes: 1) New hush sampler orchestrator (pkg/prefill/hush_sampler.go) that groups incoming requests into budget lanes (gold/silver/bronze) based on tenant heuristics and recent value signals. Each lane has an independently configurable 'quiet_rate' controlling the fraction of requests that skip expensive prefill but still receive a fast degraded path. 2) Quant hinting module (pkg/quant/hinting.go) that attaches a stable hint token to requests that pass through hush lanes. Hints are interpreted by the runtime to prefer lower-precision kernels or compact cache allocations; the runtime will fall back to full precision if quality triggers detect degradation. 3) CLI helpers and export (cmd/cli/econctl/hush_profile.go) to generate and apply hush profiles per tenant. 4) Telemetry: new prefill metrics and histograms (telemetry/prefill_metrics.yaml) and a canary workload (e2e/canaries/hush_sampler_workload.yaml) that tests economic and latency impacts. 5) Documentation and ops runbook (docs/ops/hush-sampler-runbook.md, docs/dev/quant-hinting.md) explaining configuration, safe rollouts, and playbooks for incidents. 6) Tests: unit and integration — a targeted integration (tests/integration/hush_sampler_test.go) that exercises warm/cold prefills and validation hooks. Design notes: - The hush sampler is conservative by default: quiet_rate defaults to 0.05 for bronze lanes and is tenant-scoped. - Hints are advisory and require runtime opt-in via a new capability flag. - Quality monitoring watches for hallucination and embedding drift; if diagnostic probes cross thresholds the control plane auto-elevates the lane to normal prefill behavior. Rollout plan and safety: - Feature gated behind tenant-level flags and runtime capability toggles. - Start with a shadow mode that emits metrics without changing behavior for one week (telemetry validated). - Canary on dedicated staging on region us-west-2 with a synthetic workload simulating 30% bronze traffic. - Gradual ramp: 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on metric regressions. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of hush sampler orchestrator and policy proto. - [x] Quant hinting API and runtime opt-in hooks (runtime patch submitted in separate PR). - [x] CLI and profile export/import. - [x] Telemetry and canary workloads. - [x] Docs and runbook. - [x] Unit and integration tests. Commits summary: feat(prefill): add hush sampler + policy proto; feat(quant): hinting attach/parse; test(ci): add hush canary smoke test; docs: ops runbook. Files changed (high-level): pkg/prefill/*, pkg/quant/*, cmd/cli/econctl/*, telemetry/*, docs/*, tests/integration/*. Review notes and conversation summary: - Priya Shah: "Can we ensure quiet_rate is tenant-admin controllable and visible in Console UI?" -> Response: "Yes — CLI exposes it and the Console work item (ENG-2104) is tracking the UI surface; added a note in docs." - Luca Moretti: "How do we measure downstream quality impact from quant hints?" -> Response: "Added quality probes: per-tenant hallucination-rate and embedding-similarity hooks. If probes exceed thresholds the sampler auto-escalates; thresholds are in telemetry/prefill_metrics.yaml." - Jordan Kim: "CI flake observed on integration 02, looks timing-related." -> Author: "Tightened test timeouts and restructured canary to use stable synthetic seed; reran CI — green." - Ops (feedback): "Runbook needs a command for emergency disable" -> Added `econctl hush disable --tenant <id>` in cmd/cli and documented rollback steps. CI and checks: - Unit: pass - Integration (staging): pass after one re-run - Lint: pass - Benchmarks: baseline microbenchmark shows ~12% token-cost reduction for bronze-lane workloads with <1% latency 95th percentile increase in synthetic canary. Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after reviewers approved and canary metrics validated in staging. Related work items: ENG-1890 (sampling platform), ENG-2104 (Console visibility). Follow-ups: - Runtime patch to honor quant hints and implement fallback kernel selection (PR linked in description). - UX work to expose hush profiles in Console (tracked by ENG-2104).

release_notes: Add hush-sampler: budgeted low-priority prefill lanes and quantization hinting. Reduces prefill churn for noisy low-value workloads; feature is gated and opt-in. Includes CLI, telemetry, docs, and canary. Requires runtime opt-in to use quant hints.
notes_for_qa: To exercise: enable hush sampler for a test tenant, apply default bronze profile via econctl, run the hush canary workload, and validate telemetry signals. QA should verify auto-escalation behavior by artificially tripping quality probes.
